t: Finding the Number of Visible Mountains — Sorting plus Monotonic Stack
o: Mountain with peak (x, y) spans [x-y, x+y] on the ground. Peak (px, py) lies inside mountain (x, y) iff |px - x| + py <= y. A mountain is invisible iff its peak is inside another. Sort peaks by x ascending, breaking ties by y descending; sweep with a stack: pop stack tops that the current peak hides (they have smaller height and lie within reach), and detect whether the current peak itself is hidden by the stack top. Equal duplicate peaks eliminate each other, matching example 2's answer of 0.
k: Dominance test: peak B is hidden by A iff |xB - xA| + yB <= yA.
Sorting by (x asc, y desc) lets a single stack sweep resolve all hiding relations.

a.i: After sorting, any mountain that can hide the current one must already be on the stack (larger or equal height, no greater x). Pop hidden tops; if the current peak is hidden by the new top, skip pushing it. Survivors on the stack are exactly the visible mountains.
s: Sort peaks by (x asc, y desc).
For each peak: while stack top t satisfies t.y < cur.y and |cur.x - t.x| <= cur.y - t.y, pop t.
If stack non-empty and top t satisfies t.y >= cur.y and |cur.x - t.x| <= t.y - cur.y, the current peak is hidden — do not push.
Count stack contents at the end.
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting dominates; the sweep is amortized O(n).

a.i: Transform each mountain to the interval [x-y, x+y] with height y. A peak is hidden iff some other mountain has strictly larger span containing x with sufficient height. One can compute, for each peak, whether max over mountains covering it of (y - |dx|) >= y holds using offline sweep-line with a multiset; equivalent outcome, heavier to implement.
s: At each peak x, query the maximum active (y - |dx|) contribution via a balanced structure.
Mark hidden peaks; subtract duplicates handling.
a.t: O(n log n) — same as Approach 1.

w: The sort-and-stack is the intended solution. Critical details: the tie-break (x asc, y desc) ensures identical peaks annihilate, and the hiding test uses <= (border counts as hidden). Pitfall: forgetting that a peak on another mountain's slope is NOT visible. Follow-up: report which mountains are visible, or handle circular mountains.
